questions.stem: Which part of an archive label is printed first?

explanations.a: Shelves are ordered by collection, so the code comes first.
explanations.b: The box number follows the collection code.
explanations.c: The date range comes after the box number.
explanations.d: The category is the last part of the label.

questions.stem: A box of standard records reaches its review date. What must happen before it can be destroyed?

options.text: Staff record the decision in the disposal log
The label is replaced with a new one
The box moves to the intake shelf
The box is relabelled as permanent

explanations.a: No box is destroyed without a logged decision.
explanations.b: Relabelling is for damaged labels, not disposal.
explanations.c: The intake shelf holds unreadable boxes.
explanations.d: Changing the category would not authorize destruction.

questions.stem: Why does the handbook forbid mixing retention categories in one box?

options.text: The whole box would follow the longest period
Labels have room for only one date range
Permanent records must be stored separately by law
Mixed boxes cannot be shelved by collection

explanations.a: A mixed box keeps everything for the longest period, defeating shorter categories.
explanations.b: The handbook gives a different reason.
explanations.c: The handbook does not mention legal storage rules.
explanations.d: Shelving is by collection code, not by category.
